text.p: -The Council of Europe's Parliamentary Assembly decided to postpone discussion of the Chechen crisis, yielding to the demands of the official Russian delegation at a meeting in Strasbourg, the paper says.
- Russia's negative attitude to holding a discussion of the Chechen situation at the Council of Europe's Parliamentary Assembly raised discontent among other members of the organisation.
- In its effort to solve budget problems, the Russian government has decided to cut back on customs privileges to more than 200 enterprises.
- If a new presidential election is held in Russia in the near future, it will be impossible to finance it because the country's economy is seriously damaged after the 1996 election.

- Regional elections in Russia will be a serious test for the country's democratic forces, Anatoly Chubais, the head of presidential administration, tells a congress of Russia's Democratic Choice Party.

- Protests in several Russian cities on Saturday marked the third anniversary of the "cynical and cruel coup d'etat" sparked by President Yeltsin's decree dissolving parliament, the pro-communist paper says.

- The former head of presidential security service, Alexander Korzhakov, names Alexander Lebed as the most likely successor of President Boris Yeltsin in an interview with the newspaper. -- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
